alerts.title: Carbamazepine reduces DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases dolutegravir (DTG) levels by 30-70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. The patient is on DTG with carbamazepine, which was started 2 weeks ago. The viral load is now detectable at 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence. This timing suggests the drug interaction may be causing virologic failure. The clinician's plan does not address this interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Consider switching from carbamazepine to valproic acid as per guidelines to avoid DTG level reduction.

alerts.title: Viral load >50 requires action
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend checking viral load every 6-12 months. For a viral load >50 copies/mL on a DTG-based regimen, the response should include enhanced adherence support, addressing side-effects, and repeating the viral load in 2-3 months. The patient's viral load is 1,240 copies/mL. The clinician's plan only addresses carbamazepine toxicity and is unsure of the cause for viremia, missing guideline-mandated steps for virologic monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide enhanced adherence support, address potential side-effects, and plan to repeat viral load in 2-3 months as per the algorithm.

alerts.title: Hyponatremia with carbamazepine
alerts.message: The patient has symptomatic carbamazepine toxicity (level 14 mcg/mL) with neurological signs and a low sodium of 128 mmol/L. Hyponatremia is a known adverse effect of carbamazepine. The clinician's plan to reduce the dose and repeat the level is appropriate but does not mention managing the electrolyte imbalance. Non-drug causes like SIADH should also be considered.

evidence.recommended_action: Manage hyponatremia, monitor sodium, and consider non-drug causes while adjusting carbamazepine.
